title: Execute a capped near-affine filling with exact conditional mean
statement: Given known lambda in(0,1) and supplied residual Lipschitz bound eta M for g-lambda id,the finite capped-geometric shared-replica program uses at most3 whole-vector g values every execution and preserves E[O|G]=g(G). With cap N,a^2=1-lambda^2 and paid tau reserve,it has TV(O,N(Eg(G),(1+tau^2)I))<=eta M sqrt(d)lambda^(2N+1)/(tau sqrt(2pi))+phi(1)eta^2M^2d[1+2lambda^2(1-lambda^(2N))/a^2]/tau^2.

requires: Known scalar affine reference and quantitatively small residual promise,not just a formal decomposition
Shared source for X,X prime and the same Gaussian in each endpoint pair
provides: Positive ordinary program and exact conditional mean,not only marginal mean
Actual correction second moment and full-density Taylor remainder paid
assumptions: No unbounded query loop or missing tail mass
Increasing N leaves a d eta^2 remainder
Known affine f=id has an actual positive covariance defect and TV tends to1 with d;ordinary exact affine filling is stronger
costs: At most3 original queries;optional fourth g(0) for numeric centering
O(d+N) work,O(d) storage,at most3N scalar Gaussian selector draws
Inverse weights may grow polynomially for logarithmic cap;complete bit budget unproved
One-value known-reference subtraction is stronger for marginal-only sampling but does not preserve conditional mean g(G)
contract.units: Whole-vector values,conditional filling and full marginal TV
contract.obstruction: No recurrent law contraction,seed-Lipschitz/class closure,polylog target or practical advantage.

evidence.range_scope: Bounded smooth actual first variations without strict-gauge L2 inverse,and capped three-value near-affine filling with full law.

evidence.quote: Neither return completes the general N687
evidence.range_scope: Completed separate first-return Q52=A/Q17=B audit of actual arguments/code and own replays;does not cover later continuations.

body: A coupled secant pair closes this first conditional operation. The explicit high-frequency seed-derivative growth prohibits silently reusing its original source contract.
